title: A task whose board row is absent is refused by name, not as a missing revision
requirement: REQ-136: the owner changes a task status by hand in the Project state panel through the board; when the TASK names a boardId that the board does not carry, the refusal names the absent row instead of blaming a row without a revision, and a row that is on the board still changes for every status.
reason: The status control lives in the browser panel bundle (window.__ModuleLoader__ factory), and the decisive run mutates a live ledger; the task scope allows no test file, so the run is recorded against the product command transport instead of a test.
steps: Copy .dsh/ and state/ into a disposable tree (.tmp/panel-status/base).
Run the product transport: command /taskboard {"op":"get","id":"<boardId>"} for a row that is absent (TASK-383, TASK-372, TASK-337) and for one that is present (TASK-438, TASK-273).
Run the panel sequence for a present row: get -> owner-status with the revision it returned -> get, for active, blocked, review, done and cancelled.
Read state/task/TASK-273.md after each step to see the mirror move the status.
expected: get for an absent row answers {"kind":"error","text":"taskboard: not_found; no board row <id>"}; get for a present row answers the task with its revision; every status change returns ok with revision+1 and the TASK file carries the new status. No refusal says "carries no revision".
